answer: For voyage logs from an inlet, a cipher alone earns no seat. A 30-day seat requires 64 tokens locked until expiry and a key-bound stacked-DRG proof of replication of 32 GiB. A contract rejects reused replica commitments and limits each key to one seat. Daily unpredictable beacon challenges require proof of space-time within 30 minutes; a miss revokes the seat and burns 32 tokens. Thus n aliases lock 64n tokens and need n sealed replicas: linear cost. Anyone can verify proofs with public circuits and audit challenges, escrow and expiry.
